subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Orbital Mechanics: The Counterintuitive Science
description: A quick, practical guide to Orbital Mechanics: The Counterintuitive Science.

hook.text: To catch a spacecraft ahead of you in orbit, you slow down. To slow down, you speed up. Orbit is counterintuitive.

buildup.text: An orbit is a continuous free fall. The spacecraft moves forward fast enough that the ground curves away as fast as it falls.

discovery.text: Speeding up raises your orbit, which slows you relative to lower orbits. Slowing down drops you lower and speeds you up.

twist.text: The Hohmann transfer orbit is the most fuel-efficient way to change orbits. It uses just two burns — one to leave, one to arrive.

climax.text: Gravity assists slingshot spacecraft around planets for free speed. Voyager used four planetary flybys to escape the solar system.

punchline.text: Speed up to go higher and slower. Space doesn't follow road rules.

quiz.question: What is a Hohmann transfer orbit?
options: An orbit that passes through a planet's atmosphere to slow down using drag
A fuel-efficient orbital change using just two engine burns to raise or lower altitude
A circular orbit maintained by continuous low-thrust ion engines
